title: How to Choose Konjac Powder, Refined Powder or Konjac Gum for a Food Project
description: A practical starting point for comparing konjac ingredient enquiries by application, processing conditions and specification needs.
summary: Start with the food application and the result you need, then request a grade and sample discussion against a written specification.

sections.heading: Direct answer
paragraphs: Do not choose solely from the words powder, refined powder or gum. Describe the finished food, the job the ingredient must do, the processing conditions and the specification you need. ALL KONJAC lists all three ingredient categories and discusses grade selection against the intended application. A final recommendation requires review of the actual project brief and sample results.

sections.heading: What should guide the comparison?
bullets: Application: identify the finished food and the role of the ingredient in that product.
Performance objective: describe the texture, thickening, gel formation, water holding or stability issue you want to address.
Process: record where and how the ingredient will be added, plus relevant processing conditions.
Procurement: state the requested specification, quantity, packing needs and destination market.
paragraphs: These are enquiry criteria, not a claim that one named category will perform better in every formulation. The terms refined and food grade alone do not establish a particular purity, certification or suitability for a destination market.

sections.heading: What to send for a useful ingredient discussion
bullets: Finished product and intended use.
Target texture or processing problem.
Current formula and process constraints that can be shared.
Requested specification, expected quantity, packing and destination market.
Any sample evaluation method or acceptance criteria already in use.
paragraphs: Ask for the proposed grade and its applicable specification before treating a sample as representative of a future supply arrangement. Confirm regulatory and commercial requirements for the destination market in the project discussion.

title: What to Include in a Konjac Food Equipment Project Brief
description: The information a food manufacturer should prepare before discussing an individual konjac machine or a complete production line.
summary: Describe the finished product, target output, process steps, factory conditions and the equipment that must connect to the proposed scope.

sections.heading: Direct answer
paragraphs: A useful equipment brief starts with the food you intend to make and the production task the equipment must support. ALL KONJAC accepts enquiries about individual konjac food machines and production-line integration. The existing equipment page asks for the finished product, target output, required process stages, available space, utilities and installation constraints.

sections.heading: Decisions to make before comparing configurations
bullets: Define the finished product and any relevant formulation or packaging requirements.
List the process steps the new equipment must cover and identify existing machines that will remain.
Provide a target output as a project requirement, along with operating schedule and expected variation where known.
Record the site layout, access restrictions and available utilities.
Separate requested supply, installation, commissioning and training scope.
paragraphs: A listed reference configuration is a discussion aid. It is not a promise that the same dimensions, power or arrangement will suit every factory. The final configuration and service responsibilities belong in the project quotation.

sections.heading: A short brief you can send
bullets: Finished product and target market.
Desired output and process flow.
Factory drawings, available space and utility information.
Current equipment, connection points and installation constraints.
Requested equipment and engineering service boundaries.
paragraphs: If formulation development is also needed, describe the product performance objective and processing issue so the ingredient, process and equipment discussion can be connected.

title: How to Plan a Konjac Dried-Chip Drying Line
description: A buyer's planning checklist for material preparation, conveying, drying, air handling and factory integration.
summary: Plan the drying line as a connected process around the incoming material, required dried-chip output and factory conditions.

sections.heading: Direct answer
paragraphs: Begin with the incoming konjac material, the dried-chip result required and the conditions of the factory. ALL KONJAC presents a drying-line project as an integrated process covering material preparation, conveying, drying equipment, air handling and process integration. The right configuration is determined for each project rather than from an image or a generic capacity claim.

sections.heading: What belongs in the planning brief?
bullets: Incoming material: describe its form and any preparation steps before drying.
Output requirement: state the desired dried-chip result and target production output as project requirements.
Flow: map material movement into, through and out of the dryer, including existing equipment connections.
Factory: share floor space, access, utility availability and any installation constraints.
Scope: identify which preparation, conveying, drying, air-handling and support tasks should be included.
paragraphs: Images on the site illustrate equipment or process categories. They do not establish the exact equipment configuration, dimensions, energy use or achieved drying performance for a proposed line.

sections.heading: Questions for the project discussion
bullets: Which process stages must the supplier include, and which remain with the factory?
What incoming-material and finished-product information is needed to size the line?
How will existing equipment and available utilities connect to the proposed process?
Which installation, commissioning and training tasks should appear in the quotation?
paragraphs: Use the answers to request a project-specific process and equipment proposal. Confirm performance criteria and responsibilities in that proposal rather than inferring them from a reference page.
